paper.title_en: Quadratic effective energy--momentum tensor on uniform-density hypersurfaces during slow-roll inflation
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the quadratic-order effective energy-momentum tensor (2EMT) of scalar cosmological perturbations on uniform-density hypersurfaces during slow-roll inflation. The 2EMT is a gauge-fixed effective source rather than a gauge-invariant observable. We impose the complete scalar gauge conditions $δρ=0$ and $E=0$, express all perturbations in terms of the Bardeen potential $Ψ$, and distinguish the strict infrared and ultraviolet limits from the intermediate regimes. The uniform-density time shift differs from the comoving one by an explicitly gradient-suppressed term, $Q_{\mathrm{UD}}-Q_{\mathrm{C}}=-ΔΨ/[3{\mathcal H}({\mathcal H}'-{\mathcal H}^2)]$. The two sources vanish at zero gradient, while their first nonzero infrared coefficients differ and give $w_{\rm raw}\simeq-1/3$ at leading slow-roll order. In the intermediate infrared, all four gauges have this leading ratio, with gauge-dependent amplitudes. In the ultraviolet, the longitudinal, spatially-flat, and comoving gauges give $w_{\rm raw}\simeq1/3$, whereas the uniform-density gauge gives $w_{\rm raw}\simeq1$. The common $1/ε$ enhancement of the matter-clock gauges reflects the slow evolution of their clocks; the additional uniform-density $1/σ_2^2$ enhancement originates from the Laplacian contribution to the density constraint. Neither enhancement is interpreted as a gauge-independent physical instability, and the gauge reconstruction must remain perturbatively small.
